Book.description: A book of positions and its optional strategies.

positions.description:

account limit applies (half the price batch limit for revaluation, the contract limit for a solve).

BookPosition.description:
One held option: signed quantity of contracts, each worth `multiplier`
underlying units. Its market is the request's `markets[underlying]`; its
volatility and model are its own. Net value is quantity × multiplier ×
option price, in the request `currency`.

id.description: Identifier unique within its book: 1–64 characters from A–Z, a–z, 0–9 and `. _ : / -`.

quantity.description: Signed contracts: positive long, negative short.

underlying.description:
Underlying this option is written on: the key of its market in the
request's `markets`, with the same character rules as identifiers. Not
resolved against an instrument master.

volatility.description: Annual lognormal volatility of this option, as a decimal.

BookPositionScenario.description: One position's base and shocked valuation, in the request currency.

base_unit_price.description: Option price per underlying unit at the base inputs.

contract.description: The submitted contract. With `scenario`, everything needed to replay the position.

model.description: The resolved model and its algorithm pin.

multiplier.description: Underlying units per contract, from the request.

pnl.description: shocked_net_value − base_net_value; positive means a gain.

quantity.description: Signed contracts from the request: positive long, negative short.

shocked_unit_price.description: Option price per underlying unit at the shocked inputs.

underlying.description: The position's `underlying` label from the request.

BookScenarioBook.description: One book's base and shocked valuation, in the request currency.

BookScenarioDefinition.description: A named, ordered scenario applied to every position of every book.

name.description:

shocks.description: One to 16 shocks (zero to 16 for a solve, which may not contain spot_relative).

BookShock.description:
One ordered shock. Shocks compose left to right on every position, so order
matters (a roll-down before a vol-term shock moves the tenor it reads).

oneOf.description: Multiply the underlying by 1 + relative; relative must exceed -1.

relative.description: Relative spot move as a decimal: 0.05 raises spot 5%.

oneOf.description: Add an absolute shift to volatility.

shift.description: Absolute volatility change as a decimal: 0.01 adds one volatility point.

oneOf.description:
Skew slope per unit of log-moneyness ln(K / F); positive raises
higher-strike volatility.

slope.description: Absolute volatility change per unit of ln(K / F).

oneOf.description: Add an absolute shift to the continuously compounded rate, per year.

shift.description:
Absolute change of the annual continuously compounded rate, as a
decimal (0.01 is 1%).

oneOf.description: Move the valuation later by `years` (nonnegative) with spot held.

years.description: Years to move the valuation later; nonnegative.

oneOf.description: Linear volatility ramp over remaining tenor, flat outside the anchors.

back_shift.description: Absolute volatility change applied at the back anchor, as a decimal.

back_tenor.description: Remaining tenor of the back anchor, in years.

front_shift.description: Absolute volatility change applied at the front anchor, as a decimal.

front_tenor.description:
Remaining tenor of the front anchor, in years; at least 0 and below
`back_tenor`.

contract.description: The submitted contract. With `scenario`, everything needed to replay the position.

model.description: The resolved model and its algorithm pin.

multiplier.description: Underlying units per contract, from the request.

quantity.description: Signed contracts from the request: positive long, negative short.

BookStrategy.description:
A named grouping of positions in one book. Strategies may overlap, so strategy
totals are not additive; book totals always sum positions once.

position_ids.description:
Distinct position identifiers of this book. At most 50 members (16 for
solves); at most 1,024 memberships across the request.

BookStrategyScenario.description: One strategy's member set; overlapping strategies are not additive.

base_net_value.description: Sum of the members' base_net_value, in the request currency.

shocked_net_value.description: Sum of the members' shocked_net_value, in the request currency.

BooksRevalueRequest.description:
Reprice one or more books under one composed scenario (`books.revalue`,
and the same body for `books.explain`). More than one book returns
portfolio totals. Every position costs a base and a shocked price
calculation at its model's price rate.

books.description: At most 50 books, and no more books than the position limit; total positions must fit half the account price batch limit.

currency.description:
Currency every position's prices and every total are in, e.g. USD. A
label: positions in different currencies cannot share a request, and no
conversion is applied.

markets.description: One market per underlying, at most 50.

BooksRevalueResult.description:
Book and portfolio scenario valuation. `:explain` returns exactly this result
with `attribution` added at book and portfolio level, so one parser handles both.

base_net_value.description: Sum over all books; equals the single book's totals for one book.

books.description: One entry per book of the request.

currency.description: The request currency; every amount below is in it.

pnl.description: shocked_net_value − base_net_value over all books; positive means a gain.

pnl_basis.description: Always `base_model_value`: P&L is shocked minus base modeled value.

price_evaluations.description: Price calculations performed: a base and a shocked valuation per position.

BooksSolveScenarioRequest.description:
Find every spot level at which a book's (or one strategy's) modeled P&L
equals a target (`books.solve_scenario`), under an ordered non-spot scenario. P&L
is horizon value minus `signed_reference_net_value`. Solved positions
share one underlying, so its single market's spot is the solved axis.
Roll-down may reach expiry (including engine roundoff tolerance) but not pass it.

coordinate_tolerance.description: Positive absolute spot localization tolerance; default 1e-9.

currency.description: Currency of every price and of the reference and target P&L, e.g. USD.

lower.description: Finite spot search bounds, 0 < lower < upper.

pnl_tolerance.description: Positive absolute P&L tolerance in `currency`; default 1e-6.

scenario.description:
Holding horizon and market assumptions. May not contain spot_relative:
the solve owns the spot axis.

signed_reference_net_value.description:
Net entry value subtracted from horizon value: a debit paid is positive,
a credit received is negative, in `currency`.

strategy_id.description:
Solve only this strategy's member positions instead of the whole book.
The strategy must exist and contain at least one position; validated before reservation.

target_pnl.description: Target P&L in `currency`; 0 solves for breakeven.

upper.description: Upper end of the finite spot search range; must exceed `lower`.

result.description:
Spot levels at which the solved positions' P&L meets the target, with
the search's coverage.

BooksSolveScenarioResult.description:
Spot levels at which the solved positions' P&L meets the target, with the
sign regions and coverage of the search.

book_id.description: The solved book's `id` from the request.

boundaries.description: Spot levels and ranges at which the P&L meets the target, ascending by spot.

coordinate.description: Always `spot`: a book solve searches the shared underlying level.

coverage.description: Whether every candidate the scan found was resolved.

currency.description: The request currency; P&L values and boundary `value`s are in it.

evaluations.description: P&L evaluations performed; each prices every solved position once.

positions.description: Solved positions: the whole book, or the strategy's members in order.

price_evaluations.description: Price calculations performed: (evaluations + 1) × solved positions, including base valuations.

regions.description:
Spot ranges classified by their side of the target P&L; they tile the
search range when coverage is resolved.

signed_reference_net_value.description:
The request's net entry value, in `currency`: a debit paid is positive,
a credit received is negative.

strategy_id.description: The request's `strategy_id`; absent for a whole-book solve.

underlying.description: The one underlying every solved position names.

ContractIdentity.description: The served HTTP contract: its version label and exact document digest.

sha256.description:
SHA-256 of the served HTTP contract document (`GET /openapi.json`),

version.description: API contract version label (`0.1.0` throughout the beta).

DividendEvent.description:
One discrete cash dividend.

Time is a year fraction on the same basis as `time_to_expiry_years`, not a
calendar date. The contract carries no calendar, day-count convention or
timezone, and introducing one here to express a dividend date would add a
basis the rest of the contract does not have and cannot validate. The
engine's own `DividendEvent` is `ex_time_years` for the same reason.

cash_amount.description:
Cash amount per share, in the same currency as spot and strike. Must be
positive.

ex_time_years.description:
Ex-dividend time as a year fraction from valuation. Must be positive;
events at or after expiry do not affect the price.

Greeks.description:
Available Greeks on the contract's stated bases; absent values are explained by `unavailable`.

Time derivatives are **per year**. The engine reports them per calendar
day, which embeds a 365-day calendar; the contract carries no calendar,
so the service scales by the engine's own day count at this boundary and
the caller applies whichever convention it holds. Vega is raw `dV/dσ` per
unit volatility, not per point. Nothing else is rescaled.

unavailable.description:
Each omitted Greek has a reason. A resolved zero is present as 0.0.
Codes distinguish unsupported quantities, model domain/validity,
accuracy refusals and unresolved numerical derivatives.

residual.description:

used_fallback.description:
Whether the solve left its primary path.

Not a quality signal on its own: an American solve inverts by bisection
and reports `true` for every live solve, while a Bachelier solve reports

fallback.

Finite search bounds in the coordinate's units, lower strictly below upper.

bounds lie within [0, time_to_expiry_years].

Upper end of the finite search range, in the coordinate's units; must
exceed `lower`.

inputs.description:

(boundary.value is the evaluated target quantity, not an input). Copy inputs,
then set spot = x for spot, strike = x for strike, time_to_expiry_years = x
for time_to_expiry, time_to_expiry_years = inputs.time_to_expiry_years - x
for elapsed_time, risk_free_rate = x for rate, dividend_yield = x for
dividend_yield, or volatility = x for volatility. For an interval, replay
its lower or upper coordinate by the same mapping; the interval is sampled
evidence, not a guarantee for every interior coordinate.
